Jordan / team —

Thanks for the clear asks. Below I summarized our position and the operational artifacts we will share. I tried to be precise on the retention nuances so it maps cleanly to contract language. 

What we do NOT do: 
- We do not include customer-provided content in training datasets for any production training runs. This includes fine-tuning and large-scale pretraining.
- We do not sample from customer object stores or tenant content to construct model training corpora.

What we DO collect for operations (examples and retention):
- Diagnostic telemetry (aggregate metrics, request latencies, error rates) — retained for 90 days by default; aggregated metrics stored longer (1 year) for trend analysis. No user-request payloads are included in aggregated metrics.
- Structured request logs (request metadata, timestamps, request IDs) — retained 30 days by default for debugging; can be extended by customer contract. Payloads containing user content are not retained in structured logs beyond transient debugging windows unless customer opts in.
- Snapshots & backups: 
  - Hot snapshots (short-term) — retained up to 7 days.
  - Warm snapshots (rolling monthly) — retained up to 30 days.
  - Cold/archival snapshots — retained per contract; default is 90 days and then tombstoned.
  - Backups that are retained for legal/archival reasons are isolated and not used for training or model improvement. We maintain an internal gating process; any use of archived backups for research requires an approval workflow and explicit data owner signoff.

Deletion and tombstoning flow (high level):
- Customer requests deletion via API or console -> deletion job marks objects as "tombstoned" -> background workers scrub KV caches and remove active copies -> deletion job triggers snapshot purge workflow for eligible snapshots -> we produce a deletion trace (job id + object ids + timestamps) and store that trace in the customer's evidence folder for 90 days.

Evidence we will hand over: signed No-Training Affidavit, runbook excerpt showing the tombstone and purge workflow, one redacted deletion trace (example job id and timestamps), and a pointer to our SOC 2 artifact index.

Limitations & contract language suggestions:
- If your organization requires longer archival retention for regulatory reasons, we can set an extended retention term in the contract; however, any extended backups are explicitly excluded from model training and require documented exceptions to be used for research.
- For notarization requests: we can provide an executed affidavit; notarization may require additional procurement steps and a review by Legal.

I'll attach the internal control map and a short explainer. If helpful we can also run the deletion demo against a red-team tenant during the meeting.

—Marissa
